title: SEBI Clears Path for NSE's Mega IPO With ₹1,491 Crore Settlement
excerpt: India's largest stock exchange resolves decade-old co-location dispute, removing the last regulatory barrier to what could be the country's biggest listing this year.
body:
• SEBI has granted in-principle approval for NSE to settle long-running co-location and governance cases for ₹1,491 crore ($155.8 million)
  • The settlement removes the biggest legal overhang blocking NSE's IPO, which has been delayed for nearly a decade
  • NSE filed its draft offer documents last month and has begun investor roadshows for what could be one of India's two mega IPOs this year alongside Reliance Jio
  • NSE reported ₹18,700 crore in total income and ₹10,302 crore net profit for FY2026, with a 53% net margin

A Decade-Long Dispute Nears Resolution

India's National Stock Exchange cleared its biggest regulatory hurdle on Thursday when the Securities and Exchange Board of India agreed in principle to settle the co-location and governance cases that have blocked the exchange's public listing since 2016.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Ar_b_u7TMI0

NSE's auditor disclosed in the exchange's quarterly results report that SEBI had accepted a proposed settlement payment of ₹1,491 crore ($155.83 million), according to Reuters. The cases centered on allegations that the exchange failed to provide equitable access to all trading members through its co-location facility — where traders place servers close to the exchange's matching engine for faster execution — and related governance lapses.

"The settlement removes the biggest legal overhang facing the exchange as it prepares for an IPO later this year."

— Reuters

SEBI originally fined NSE ₹1,100 crore in 2019, a penalty the exchange challenged in the Securities Appellate Tribunal. Parts of SEBI's order were set aside, but the regulator appealed to the Supreme Court, creating a legal tangle that froze listing plans. The settlement, which does not require NSE to admit wrongdoing, now awaits review by SEBI's Internal Committee and High-Powered Advisory Committee before a final closure order.

IPO Roadshow Already Underway

NSE filed its draft offer documents with SEBI last month, appointing 20 investment banks — the most ever for an Indian public issue — to manage the offering. Investor roadshows are already underway, and banks have sent letters to existing shareholders inviting expressions of interest to sell their stakes.

The exchange is expected to be one of India's two mega IPOs this year, alongside billionaire Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Jio. NSE's current shareholder roster includes the Life Insurance Corporation of India (10.72%), State Bank of India (7.76%), Canada Pension Plan Investment Board (1.60%), and Morgan Stanley (1.58%). Its domestic rival, BSE Ltd, listed in 2017.

A Profit Machine Waiting to List

NSE's financials underscore why the IPO has drawn such anticipation. The exchange reported ₹18,700 crore ($1.98 billion) in total income and ₹10,302 crore in net profit for the year ending March 2026, translating to a 53% net margin. Transaction charges account for roughly 82% of revenue, driven by NSE's dominant position in India's derivatives market, where it operates as the world's most active exchange by contract volume.

Trading volumes did take a hit after SEBI introduced measures last year to cool India's derivatives frenzy. Average daily options volume by premium fell 16% quarter-on-quarter in late 2025 after the regulator raised lot sizes and margin requirements. But NSE's sheer scale — it has approximately 190,000 investors as an unlisted company — means the listing remains one of the most closely watched events in Indian capital markets.

What's Next

The settlement still needs Supreme Court sign-off, since SEBI itself challenged an earlier SAT ruling before the apex court. Legal experts say the regulator cannot treat this as a purely administrative exercise without judicial clearance. If all goes according to the expected timeline, the IPO could hit markets before the end of 2026, giving India's estimated 150 million retail investors a chance to own a piece of the infrastructure they trade on every day.
nri_angle: NSE's IPO would give NRI investors direct ownership in India's primary trading infrastructure, while the exchange's derivatives volume directly affects portfolio hedging strategies.
